title: Fats selling air plugs to publishers by the checkbook
summary: Fats sold songs for whiskey money and asked publishers for their checkbooks before broadcasting their tunes, but plugged a loyal little publisher free.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Yep. Yeah, see, so they came in, and one particular story -- this knocked me out, man, because I don't know, I like people being people.

So this particular man -- I forget his name, I've forgotten his name -- who's a publisher, but he had been very good to Fats down through the years. Well I know you've heard the story about Fats. Fats could write a tune on toilet paper and sell it. And most times he did, because he wanted some money to buy some whiskey while he was downtown, he'd walk in any place and say Give me $50.00. And say Give it to me. Give it to me. You know. And he'd go right downstairs in the bar somewhere with the gang, and they would drink up.
You know, and sometimes they'd have a song title written on the paper, I mean, you know, whatever it was. So

the guys came in, and they would -- Hey Fats, (unintelligible) you're on the air do this for me. You broadcast, (unintelligible). Pats say, different guys, he'd say, yes, I remember you, I remember you, and wait a minute, you want this on the air? Yeah, well yes, Fats, he say how bad do you want it on the -- let me see your checkbook?
Oh, so they'd start reaching in their pocket, writing checks, you know. (Laughs.)

Okay, Fats, Okay. So a lot of them came to me, just two or three of them came, Hey Herman, could you help? Get Fats to do it. I'd say well, I don't know, well they're asking me a favor. I say I'll see what I can do! (Laughs.) Which I never mentioned to him, because he and I was supposed to be good friends by this --

And that's -- see, I learned that from looking and listening. So Fats accepted money from several. He pointed to his one man, and he say you, you don't need a dime. He say you haven't got enough money to pay me. He say you've been good to me for many years, he say, anything you bring in here I'll do it and it won't cost you a nickle. The man started crying.
He said Fats, thanks. He say no, you have done -- you -- a lot of nice things for me. Say oh, what you heard me
telling them, don't go for over you. Anything you want played, bring it in and I'll play it for you, and don't worry about any money.
